chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Umar ibn Ma'mar ibn Ata' ibn Washika, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The people will not be set right regarding divorce except by the sword, and if I were their guardian I would return them to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الطَّلَاق: Divorce (talaq): the Islamic legal dissolution of marriage, governed by strict Quranic rules in Surah al-Baqarah 2:229-232 and Surah al-Talaq 65:1-7
key_terms.بِالسَّيْف: By the sword: metaphor for coercive authority and enforcement; signifies that only the legitimate Imam's rule could correct the widespread deviation
key_terms.كِتَاب اللَّه: The Book of Allah: the Quran, whose divorce rulings were being violated
key_terms.وَلِيتُهُم: If I were their guardian/wali: refers to the Imam's claim to rightful political and religious authority (wilaya) over the Muslim community

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about people's deviation from Quranic divorce laws?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delivered a striking declaration about the widespread corruption in divorce practices among the Muslim community of his era. He stated that people had deviated so far from Quranic divorce laws that only coercive enforcement ('the sword') could correct them. The Imam added that if he were the legitimate ruler (wali) over them, he would enforce a return to the Book of Allah — indicating both his rightful authority and the severity of the deviation from divine law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Umar Bin Ma’mar Bni Ata’ie Bin Washeyka who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: The people would not be corrected regarding the divorce except by the sword, and if Iasws were to be taken as a Wali (guardian) them, Iasws would return them to the Book of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Umar ibn Mu’ammar ibn’Ata’ ibn Washik who has said the following: “

I once heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘In matters of divorce people do not behave properly without the sword. Had I been governing them I would return them to the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
